title: A localization with enough projective representatives computes left derived functors
statement:
Work in fixed universes [def-weil-size-convention], enlarged to contain the categories and functor categories below. Let $C,D,H$ be categories and $W$ a class of arrows of $C$. Let $Q:C\to D$ be an essentially surjective localization at $W$: precomposition with $Q$ is fully faithful on functor categories, with essential image the functors that send every arrow in $W$ to an isomorphism. Let $\mathcal P$ be a class of objects of $C$. Assume (i) for every $X\in C$ there are $P_X\in\mathcal P$ and $q_X:P_X\to X$ such that $Q(q_X)$ is an isomorphism; (ii) for every $P\in\mathcal P$ and every $X\in C$, the map induced by $Q$ is a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_C(P,X)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_D(QP,QX).$$
For any functor $F:C\to H$ there exist a functor $LF:D\to H$ and a natural transformation $\varepsilon:LF\circ Q\to F$ with the following universal property: for every $G:D\to H$, composition with $\varepsilon$ gives a bijection
$$\operatorname{Nat}(G,LF)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Nat}(G\circ Q,F),\qquad \beta\longmapsto\varepsilon\circ(\beta Q).$$
For every pair $(LF,\varepsilon)$ with this universal property and every $P\in\mathcal P$, the component $\varepsilon_P:LF(QP)\to F(P)$ is an isomorphism. In particular these components give a natural isomorphism on the full subcategory of $C$ on $\mathcal P$: for $f:P\to P'$ one has $\varepsilon_{P'}\circ LF(Qf)=F(f)\circ\varepsilon_P$.

proof.text: Fix $Y\in D$. Essential surjectivity gives $X\in C$ and an isomorphism $u:Y\xrightarrow{\sim}QX$; choose $q:P\to X$ as in (i), and put $a=(Qq)^{-1}\circ u:Y\xrightarrow{\sim}QP$. In the comma category $J_Y$ of [lem-sfb-pointwise-right-kan-from-limits], $(P,a)$ is initial: a map to $(Z,b)$ is exactly $f:P\to Z$ with $Qf=b\circ a^{-1}$. Hypothesis (ii), applied to $P,Z$, gives exactly one such $f$.

proof.text: For $T_Y$ as in [lem-sfb-pointwise-right-kan-from-limits], let $j_0=(P,a)$ be this initial object and $i_j:j_0\to j$ its unique arrows. The cone with vertex $F(P)$ and legs $T_Y(i_j)$ is limiting: a cone $(V,v_j)$ factors by $v_{j_0}$, because $T_Y(i_j)v_{j_0}=v_j$; this factor is unique since $i_{j_0}=1$. Thus every required limit exists, without assuming that $H$ has any other limits.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-pointwise-right-kan-from-limits] to these comma-diagram limits. It gives $L_0:D\to H$ and $e_0:L_0Q\to F$ with the asserted bijection for every $G$, and with $(e_0)_X$ the projection indexed by $(X,1_{QX})$. This proves the existence clause.

proof.text: For $P\in\mathcal P$, the object $(P,1_{QP})$ is itself initial in $J_{QP}$: a map to $(Z,b)$ is the unique lift of $b$ supplied by (ii). For any limiting cone $(V,v_j)$ on $T_{QP}$, form the cone with vertex $F(P)$ and legs $T_{QP}(i_j)$. Its unique map $t:F(P)\to V$ satisfies $v_{j_0}t=1$; moreover $v_j t v_{j_0}=T_{QP}(i_j)v_{j_0}=v_j$ for every $j$, so limit uniqueness gives $t v_{j_0}=1$. By the counit formula in [lem-sfb-pointwise-right-kan-from-limits], $v_{j_0}=(e_0)_P$, hence this component is invertible.

source.place: Tag 06XN, lemma-find-existence-computes (dual conclusion); agent generalization to arbitrary categories via explicit comma limits, compared with Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Functor/KanExtension/Pointwise.lean:709-764

proof.text: Let $(LF,\varepsilon)$ be any pair with the stated universal property. Apply [lem-sfb-right-kan-extension-unique-iso] to $(LF,\varepsilon)$ and $(L_0,e_0)$, obtaining an isomorphism $v:LF\xrightarrow{\sim}L_0$ with $\varepsilon=e_0\circ(vQ)$. At $P\in\mathcal P$ this is a composite of two isomorphisms, so $\varepsilon_P$ is invertible. Naturality of $\varepsilon$ at $f:P\to P'$ is exactly $\varepsilon_{P'}\circ LF(Qf)=F(f)\circ\varepsilon_P$. The component inverses obey the inverse naturality equation by multiplying this equality by those inverses, giving the natural isomorphism on the full subcategory on $\mathcal P$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_leftDerived_of_projective_localization {C : Type uC} [Category.{vC} C] {D : Type uD} [Category.{vD} D] {H : Type uH} [Category.{vH} H] (W : MorphismProperty C) (Q : C ⥤ D) [Q.IsLocalization W] (S : ObjectProperty C) (hrep : ∀ X : C, ∃ P : C, S P ∧ ∃ q : P ⟶ X, IsIso (Q.map q)) (hhom : ∀ (P X : C), S P → Function.Bijective (Q.map : (P ⟶ X) → (Q.obj P ⟶ Q.obj X))) (F : C ⥤ H) : (∃ (LF : D ⥤ H) (ε : Q ⋙ LF ⟶ F), ∀ G : D ⥤ H, Function.Bijective (fun β : G ⟶ LF ↦ Functor.whiskerLeft Q β ≫ ε)) ∧ (∀ (LF : D ⥤ H) (ε : Q ⋙ LF ⟶ F), (∀ G : D ⥤ H, Function.Bijective (fun β : G ⟶ LF ↦ Functor.whiskerLeft Q β ≫ ε)) → (∀ P : C, S P → IsIso (ε.app P)) ∧ IsIso (Functor.whiskerLeft S.ι ε) ∧ ∀ (P P' : C), S P → S P' → ∀ f : P ⟶ P', LF.map (Q.map f) ≫ ε.app P' = ε.app P ≫ F.map f)
